rv.q: Lear deBessonet's staging of A Midsummer Night's Dream is a delightfully frothy theatrical palate cleanser that will prove a balm to theatergoers weary of controversy.
In 'Midsummer,' though, that has its drawbacks.
This Midsummer is not so much play as pageant, a Technicolor mishmash of styles, gestures, sounds, and ideas that, for the most part, have little discernible relation to one another.

Less successful is Kristine Nielsen’s trickster Puck, whose mugging recalls one of those one of those sitcom characters like Urkel forced to rely on catchphrases and double-takes late in a series’ run.
